speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to better understand the underlying cause, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient mentions the symptoms started "recently" and notes clumsiness on the right side. To determine if this is a progressive neurodegenerative condition or an acute structural lesion, could you please specify your age and any history of trauma, tumors, or recent infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

I have identified the high-risk combination of Crohn's disease, natalizumab use, and new onset ataxia. This clinical picture is highly suggestive of an opportunistic infection of the central nervous system. Are you currently experiencing any new cognitive changes, vision problems, or weakness in your limbs?
